questions.text: The DNS maps the IP address to
questions.solution:
DNS links IP addresses with names that are organised in a hierarchy (e.g. www.example.com: com [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] example [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] www).

Answer: A hierarchy of domain names

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?
questions.solution:
A cookie is a small piece of data (name-value text) stored by the browser, not executable code.

It does come in the Set-Cookie HTTP header, has an expiry time and can track browsing on a site.

Answer: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise security

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user's work area through an HTTP header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site

questions.text: In one of the pairs of protocols given below, both the protocols can use multiple TCP connections between the same client and the server. Which one is that?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP: a browser can open several parallel TCP connections to the same server.
- FTP: uses a control connection plus separate data connections.

TELNET and SMTP use a single connection.

Answer: HTTP, FTP

questions.text: Suppose you are browsing the world wide web using a web browser and trying to access the web servers. What is the underlying protocol and port number that are being used?
questions.solution:
HTTP runs over TCP on port 80. (Port 25 is SMTP.)

Answer: TCP, 80

questions.text:
A graphical HTML browser resident at a network client machine Q accesses a static HTML
webpage from a HTTP server S. The static HTML page has exactly one static embedded
image which is also at S. Assuming no caching, which one of the following is correct about
the HTML webpage loading (including the embedded image)?
questions.solution:
The HTML page and the embedded image are two separate objects, so at least 2 HTTP GET requests are needed.

With persistent HTTP (keep-alive), both requests can be sent over one TCP connection.

Answer: Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, but a single TCP connection is sufficient

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options:
Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, each necessarily in a separate TCP
connection to server S
Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, but a single TCP connection to server S is sufficient
A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and a single TCP connection between Q and S is necessary for this
A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and this is possible without any TCP connection between Q and S
